clue.text: There's a place and time for destructive pest

parts.note: a locus is a place or position, from the Latin

explanation.surface: A warning that there is a right moment and setting for a ruinous pest.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect swarms in plagues that strip crops bare, the classic destroyer of harvests.

clue.text: Name of man to be captured by soldiers

indicators.note: something captured is held within its captors, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the crossword stand-in for ordinary soldiers
to live is to exist, to be

explanation.surface: A man's name is to be taken prisoner by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's given name, as in the Dickens orphan Twist.

clue.text: Charge less for meat, including fillet

definitions.meaning: to price below a rival is to sell more cheaply than them
the underside of a sirloin of beef, which holds the fillet, has this butchery name

explanation.surface: A butcher cuts the price of beef, fillet included.
explanation.definitionFit: Pricing below a competitor and the butcher's name for the underside cut of beef sirloin share this one word.

clue.text: Alarming line in cable holding up journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey
a cable is a wire

explanation.surface: A line in a cable has stalled someone's travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wire that sets off an alarm or trap when a foot catches it is literally an alarming line.

clue.text: As fruit, chap's eaten one apple

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a chap is a man; the 's stands for has
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten an apple is treated as fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old English variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Convict dividing heap of plunder

indicators.note: a piece that divides another splits it open by sitting in its middle

parts.note: a pile is a heap
a lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner shares out a pile of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean the violent seizing of goods, as by soldiers sacking a town.

clue.text: Lecher involving European in chancy activity

indicators.note: to involve here is to enclose, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a lecher
a Lett is a Latvian, so a European

explanation.surface: A womaniser draws a fellow European into a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino wheel game is pure gambling, an activity governed by chance.

clue.text: Entering a slope, securely fasten climber

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, going inside it

parts.note: to list is to lean or slope, as a ship does
to pin is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: A mountaineer heads up a slope and makes fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer, especially in high mountains like the Alps.

clue.text: Practical decision not to attempt Lear?

definitions.meaning: down-to-earth and businesslike, with no fuss
Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse, so refusing to try it is deciding against nonsense

explanation.surface: A sensible decision not to stage King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear looks like Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear, the Victorian writer of nonsense rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with this hyphenated label is plain and practical, tolerating no foolishness.

clue.text: Turn and fight for one attacked by Don

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as a handle
a mill is old slang for a fistfight

explanation.surface: A call to twist and struggle on behalf of a victim of a university don.
explanation.walkthrough: Don is not a lecturer but Don Quixote, who tilted at these, thinking them giants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes' knight famously charged at these sails believing them to be giants.

clue.text: Points put to casual workers uninterested in politics

indicators.note: one piece is put next to the other, following it

parts.note: the lump is British slang for self-employed casual building workers
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Tips handed to temporary staff who do not care about politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marxist term lumpenproletariat named the underclass seen as indifferent to political consciousness.

clue.text: Name in a longer form

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
to form letters anew is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A name written out in its fuller version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges A LONGER into ALGERON, and N goes inside it. The whole clue is the definition too: Algy is short for this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Algy is the familiar short form of this man's name, so the full version is a longer form.

clue.text: Breaking out of cold storage

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps
racking is a framework of shelves used for storage

explanation.surface: Something breaks free of refrigeration.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting or fracturing, as ice or a cup does, is breaking.

clue.text: Film the White House for Hispanic audience

definitions.meaning: the 1942 Bogart and Bergman wartime classic

definitions.text: the White House for Hispanic audience
definitions.meaning: the phrase put into Spanish for Spanish speakers, casa being house and blanca white

explanation.surface: A movie about the US president's home aimed at Spanish-speaking viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bogart film takes its title from the Moroccan city whose Spanish name means white house.

clue.text: Officer's different way to kill

parts.note: SM is a Sergeant Major, a senior non-commissioned officer
otherwise, in another way, is other

explanation.surface: An officer has a novel method of murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate someone by covering the face is a method of killing.

clue.text: It's no use now to be away, having arranged to meet

parts.note: out means away, not at home
dated means having made a date with someone

explanation.surface: Having made a date while away is now pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete has passed its useful time and is no longer of service.

clue.text: Recklessly determined he will be new Tory leader

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man is set on becoming the next Conservative party chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something at all costs, regardless of consequences, is to be utterly resolved and reckless.

clue.text: Pacify with small gun taken out

indicators.note: the gun is opened out to take something within it

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Calm someone by removing a small firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To mollify or soothe someone, making them more agreeable, as if adding sugar.

clue.text: Hit with rope and worsted

parts.note: to whip is to hit
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: Someone struck with a rope and beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worsted' reads as beaten, but it is the woollen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tough twilled worsted fabric with a ribbed weave.

clue.text: Unusually intense physicist, at heart

indicators.note: letters that behave unusually are set out in an unexpected order
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A remarkably fierce scientist, deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges INTENSE plus I, the middle letter of 'physicist'. The whole clue also defines: a physicist with I at his heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-born scientist behind relativity is the most famous physicist of all.

clue.text: Requiring firm application to make steady progress

definitions.meaning: describing stickers or nails that adhere when pushed down

explanation.surface: Something that needs pressing hard if it is to advance steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure-applied items stick when pushed firmly, and continuing resolutely is the phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: Start firing again — as a rule, it leads to end of peace

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Hostilities resume, since as a rule disorder ends peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle anew or restart an engine, or to resume fire.

clue.text: Island excessively full of game taken by sportsmen

indicators.note: the outer piece is full of the inner, holding it inside

parts.note: too means excessively
a bag is the total of game shot by hunters

explanation.surface: Hunters take too much game on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Caribbean island paired with Trinidad.

clue.text: After transformation, alley kid is refined

indicators.note: letters transformed are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A street urchin, transformed, becomes genteel.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel and well-mannered behaviour is what a lady is supposed to show.

clue.text: New number is lower

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs, like the old anaesthetic ether

explanation.surface: A new figure is smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective means under or below, as in the underworld regions.

clue.text: Worker in depot turned out a monster

indicators.note: the letters are turned out into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A warehouse employee proved to be a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in charge of the stock in a warehouse or stores.

clue.text: Heartless audience reaction in show trial

indicators.note: the middle of the two-word phrase is cut away, leaving only its beginning and end

explanation.surface: A muted crowd response at a political show trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show trial' suggests a political frame-up but is a performer's try-out. 'Heartless' removes the middle ENCE REAC from 'audience reaction'.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's tryout, a trial of their ability to perform, is held before casting.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader initially depicted by Chekhov

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Anton is the first name of the Russian playwright Chekhov

explanation.surface: A revolutionary portrayed first by a Russian playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Danton led the French Revolution before being guillotined in the Terror.
